    World Health Organisation Global Influenza Programme for Australia

    Source: R/data.R
    influenza.Rd

    Influenza-like illness data were retrieved from the World Health Organization’s Global Influenza Programme for Australia, and subset to the weeks starting January 2, 2012 to February 24, 2020, before the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted influenza transmission and surveillance. The data described: (1) the weekly number of cases of influenza-like illness; and (2) the weekly number of laboratory specimens tested, and of those positive for influenza by type and subtype. The specimen counts come from laboratory surveillance separate from the influenza-like illness counts, and are not a subset of them. We grouped the specimens into: influenza A (all influenza A positives, whether or not subtyped), of which some were subtyped as influenza A H3N2 or influenza A H1N1 (influenza A H1N1, influenza A H1N1pdm09); influenza B (influenza B Yamagata, influenza B Victoria, influenza B lineage not determined); and other (specimens tested that were not positive for influenza).

    Usage

    influenza

    Format

    influenza

    A data frame with 426 rows and 7 columns:

    ili

    Integer, weekly number of cases of influenza-like illness

    week

    Date, start of the week, from 2 January 2012 to 24 February 2020

    inf_A

    Integer, weekly number of specimens positive for influenza A, including those subsequently subtyped as H3N2 or H1N1

    inf_B

    Integer, weekly number of specimens positive for influenza B

    inf_H3N2

    Integer, weekly number of specimens positive for influenza A subtype H3N2

    inf_H1N1

    Integer, weekly number of specimens positive for influenza A subtype H1N1

    other

    Integer, weekly number of specimens tested that were not positive for influenza, calculated as the number of specimens tested minus the number positive for influenza A or B

    Source

    https://www.who.int/teams/global-influenza-programme/surveillance-and-monitoring/influenza-surveillance-outputs
